Hi Priya — congrats and thanks for starting this early. A few procedural notes so we can get this formalized quickly: 

1) Documentation: we need a dated medical note that indicates (a) expected delivery date, (b) recommended duration of reduced hours, and (c) any medical restrictions if relevant (lifting, night shifts, etc.). The draft you attached is fine as a start but please have the clinician sign or provide a clinic letter.

2) Forms & approvals: I will send the official Return-to-Work / Temporary Accommodation form via DocuSign. We require manager sign-off (Logan) + HR sign-off. The DocuSign link: https://redwood.docusign.com/recipient/RETURN_TO_WORK_FORM

3) Payroll & benefits: Payroll can process temporary FTE adjustments; please note that partial FTE affects pro-rated vacation accrual and short-term disability (if elected). I'll flag Payroll to expect a change for July and August.

4) Timeframe & on-call: we can document a 6-week window with an explicit start date (actual start = date you confirm you're ready to resume full hours). Manager needs to specify emergency contact protocol if an urgent incident requires your attention.

5) Coverage docs: if you can share the coverage matrix (spreadsheet) with task owners, I'll attach it to the DocuSign packet as evidence of operational continuity.

I'll attach the HR guidance PDF and the sample coverage matrix for editing. Let me know when you want the DocuSign sent.

Best,
Laura Bennett
People Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
